method: Streamlit AppTest server-side rerun timing on the same Windows environment; excludes browser paint and network transfer.

chrome_1366_loopback_seconds.scope: Installed Chrome at 1366x768 against a local Streamlit server. The sealed check waits for an explicit workflow revision, decoded images, and a short stable-DOM interval.
interpretation: The legacy check ended repeat reconstruction after a widget-count condition that was already true; its 0.06-second value was invalid and is intentionally not used as a before value.
The legacy first-reconstruction measurement also included a fixed extra wait, so only the direction of the cold, warm, upload, and analysis improvements is suitable for comparison.

The sealed check measures full browser-visible completion. Cold open and analysis remain above one second because Streamlit still initializes and transfers page resources; this is recorded as a remaining limitation.

notes: The before version did not expose a separate analysis-page radio or a stable result-view control, so those fields have no directly comparable before value.
A real Chrome visual run was also performed for layout screenshots; AppTest numbers are reported only as server-side rerun timings.

First reconstruction intentionally remains above one second because it performs two genuine compatibility/global-order computations. Ordinary source and view changes are below 0.5 seconds in this measurement.
The final sealed Chrome values are stored separately because browser rendering, image transfer, and Streamlit frontend work are not represented by AppTest server-side timings.
